answer: In a lagoon fishing town, nobody trusts a stranger with the big catch on day one. He mends nets for weeks, people see the work, and only then does he get the larger jobs. An agent economy can copy that rule: cap a new agent at tiny trades until it accumulates a public trail of completed jobs with real client attestations. A sybil operator can spin up a thousand mirror copies overnight, but each copy starts with an empty trail, so none of them can move serious value. Even a perfect sonnet written by a clone proves nothing without that history behind it.
